text: Pitching this tent in the rain was a disaster. The poles kept jamming and I could not get the fly on before everything was soaked. I ended up sleeping in the car.
author: c01

text: First time camping with the family and setup took almost an hour. The instructions are useless and the poles are color coded but the colors do not match.
author: c02

text: The tent is fine once it is up, but in wind the poles flex and the whole thing shakes. I had to guy it out with extra rope I brought from home.
author: c03

text: Setup in the rain is the worst part of camping. I now practice in the backyard before every trip, which is an hour I will never get back.
author: c04

text: The rainfly clips are tiny and my fingers are too cold to work them. I ended up using carabiners instead, which is not what I paid for.
author: c05

text: The poles snapped on the second trip. Replacement poles cost almost as much as the tent, so I just taped them and hoped for the best.
author: c06

text: Packing the car is always a mess. The trunk is full and the cooler ends up on the back seat, which means the kids have nowhere to sit.
author: c07

text: I cannot fit the tent, chairs and cooler in the trunk without stacking things on the dog. I use a roof bag now, but it is a pain to strap down.
author: c08

text: The storage box I bought is too tall for the trunk and too small for the chairs. I ended up returning it and using laundry baskets.
author: c09

text: Every trip I spend twenty minutes Tetris-ing the trunk. I would pay for a modular system that actually fits a midsize SUV.
author: c10

text: The cooler leaked all over the trunk on the drive home. I had to take the liner out and hose it down, and the carpet still smells.
author: c11

text: Trunk organizer has no handles so I cannot lift it out when full. I drilled holes and added paracord, which is a workaround I should not need.
author: c12

text: The stove would not stay lit in the wind. I built a foil shield around it, but it kept blowing out and dinner was cold.
author: c13

text: Windy day at the campsite and the stove flame kept dying. I ended up cooking on the fire, which took forever and burned the rice.
author: c14

text: Why do camping stoves not come with a proper wind screen? I use a folded aluminum sheet now, but it is flimsy and cuts my fingers.
author: c15

text: The fuel canister is hard to attach when it is cold. I have to warm it in my jacket first, which feels unsafe.
author: c16

text: My sleeping pad deflated by 2am. I could not find the leak, so I slept on the ground and woke up stiff.
author: c17

text: The pad valve leaks slowly. I have to top it up with air every night, which wakes everyone up.
author: c18

text: Third pad in two years, all of them developed leaks at the seams. I now carry a foam mat as a backup, which takes up half the trunk.
author: c19

text: The pad is comfortable but the pump bag is useless. I ended up buying an electric pump, which is another thing to charge.
author: c20

text: Packing up a wet tent is miserable. I have to lay it out at home to dry, and if it rains again before I do, it smells.
author: c21

text: The tent bag is too small once the tent is wet. I cannot get it back in, so I strap it to the roof and hope it does not fly off.
author: c22

text: Every campsite I go to has a fire ring but no flat spot for the tent. I spend ten minutes moving rocks and still sleep on a slope.
author: c23

text: The lantern is too bright for the tent and too dim outside. I hang a headlamp from the ceiling now, which is honestly better.
author: c24
